commit_message:
lavc/dvx: use texdsp funcs for texture block decompression

Signed-off-by: Connor Worley <connorbworley@gmail.com>
pr_title: lavc/dvx: use texdsp funcs for texture block decompression

fix_commit.message: avcodec/dxv: Check coded_height, to avoid invalid av_clip()
fix_commit.author: Michael Niedermayer

findings.title: Missing validation of coded_height before av_clip() min/max computation in dxv_decode
findings.message: In dxv_decode(), the slice_count values for the texdsp and chroma-texdsp decompression contexts are computed with av_clip(avctx->thread_count, 1, avctx->coded_height / TEXTURE_BLOCK_H) and av_clip(avctx->thread_count, 1, cavctx.coded_height / TEXTURE_BLOCK_H). TEXTURE_BLOCK_H is 4. If avctx->coded_height (or cavctx.coded_height, which is coded_height/2 for chroma-planar formats) is smaller than TEXTURE_BLOCK_H, the integer division truncates to 0, so av_clip() is called with min=1 and max=0. Since min > max, this violates av_clip()'s precondition (asserted via av_assert2(min <= max) inside the av_clip family of inline helpers), triggering an assertion failure/undefined behavior when running a debug build, and producing bogus slice_count values (later clamped by av_clip's internal min()/max() ordering) that can lead to bad slice boundary math in downstream decompression threads for malformed/pathological input where the coded height is very small (e.g. produced via a crafted DXV bitstream where header width/height yield a tiny coded_height, or FFALIGN rounding still leaves height < TEXTURE_BLOCK_H for certain formats). No check exists to ensure coded_height (or the halved coded_height used for chroma planes in YCG6/YG10 formats) is large enough before this computation.
findings.suggestion: Before computing texdsp_ctx.slice_count and ctexdsp_ctx.slice_count, verify that avctx->coded_height / TEXTURE_BLOCK_H (and, for the chroma path, cavctx.coded_height / TEXTURE_BLOCK_H, i.e. avctx->coded_height / 2 / TEXTURE_BLOCK_H) is at least 1, returning AVERROR_INVALIDDATA otherwise, so av_clip() is never called with a max value less than its min value of 1.

ground_truth.root_cause: The refactor that introduced texdsp_ctx-based slice_count computation (replacing the previous FFMAX(ctx->texture_block_h, ctx->ctexture_block_h) based divisor) did not add a guard ensuring the coded_height-derived divisor used in av_clip()'s max argument is >= 1 before calling av_clip(), allowing pathological small coded_height values from attacker-controlled input to violate av_clip()'s min<=max invariant.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Missing validation of coded_height before av_clip() min/max computation in dxv_decode
